hero: This family clusters into two editorial modes. BERGEN and Mokat open with oversized-type, magazine-cover heroes: a very large display headline (name or one-line statement) set at near-viewport scale, minimal chrome, the role as a small caption beneath — masthead logic where type IS the hero and no image is needed for the first-5s credibility. Lucide and Teo open calmer: a restrained headline plus a short positioning sentence over generous whitespace, then a storytelling grid of selected work; credibility comes from typographic rhythm and pacing, not logos or motion. Across all four the hero states identity in words at large scale rather than leaning on a photo or 3D flourish. [uncertain] exact per-template copy not verified pixel-for-pixel.
wordmark_identity: Name-as-logotype in the top-left nav, plain grotesque sans, no graphic mark — identity carried by type weight, tracking, and scale rather than a symbol. BERGEN/Mokat push the name to oversized editorial scale so the wordmark doubles as a display element; Lucide/Teo keep it a quiet nav-corner logotype. Directly relevant to the Madhavi 'Madhavi' wordmark: set the name in the display serif at scale and let the ECG glyph be the only mark. No monogram/ligature pattern observed in these templates [uncertain].
signature_detail: These are template systems, so the ownable element is a reusable layout device rather than a personal glyph: BERGEN/Mokat's signature is the oversized-type magazine spread (headline breaking the grid, full-bleed alternating with wide-tracked captions); Lucide/Teo's signature is a disciplined storytelling grid with strong vertical rhythm. None ship a bespoke ownable mark (that is the gap Madhavi fills with the ECG). The stealable idea: one consistent editorial device (oversized headline + caption metadata) applied uniformly so pages read as one issue. [uncertain] no single recurring glyph.
typography: The core reason to study this family. All lean type-first: large neo-grotesque/grotesque display faces (BERGEN/Mokat run extreme scale jumps, tight leading, uppercase runs, wide letter-spacing as an expressive device); Lucide/Teo use a cleaner sans system with a strong big-to-small scale and generous line-height for reading. Magazine-spread project pages set body in a comfortable measure with oversized section headings. No explicit Fraunces/Inter pairing observed [uncertain] — but the pattern to steal is the extreme scale contrast (huge display heading -> mid body -> tiny wide-tracked metadata caption), which maps cleanly onto a Fraunces-display + Inter-body system.
whitespace_layout: Generous margins and a disciplined magazine grid throughout. BERGEN/Mokat alternate full-bleed media with narrow captioned text blocks and let headlines break the grid for drama; Lucide/Teo achieve 'designed not templated' through very generous whitespace, a simple aligned work grid, and deliberate vertical rhythm. Reading width for prose held narrow/centered; index/galleries widen out. Strong page-turn pacing carries the eye down. This matches Brand_Kit's generous-whitespace + 96px section rhythm + 672px prose / 1200px index model.
color_accent_discipline: Predominantly near-monochrome editorial palettes (black/off-white) with photography or a single accent supplying colour — a clean model for maroon-as-sole-accent. BERGEN/Mokat let type and imagery carry the page with minimal standing colour; Lucide/Teo similarly restrained. Some Webflow editorial templates ship a bolder accent, but the reusable discipline here is 'type and whitespace do the work, accent is a seasoning' — directly compatible with the <5%-of-visual-field maroon rule. [uncertain] exact default accent hues vary per template.
light_dark_tone: Ship light-mode editorial by default (dark type on off-white). Dark variants exist in the broader Webflow editorial template pool but are not the defining trait of these four [uncertain]. None strongly demonstrate a single-accent-holds-across-themes token system; the maroon-across-light/dark pattern is better sourced from Comeau's semantic-token approach than from these templates.
motion: Restrained, Webflow-native interactions: opacity + small translate reveals on scroll, staged section entrances, occasional oversized-type marquee or horizontal scroll for the work index. BERGEN/Mokat use editorial scroll pacing (image/caption reveals reinforcing the 'issue' rhythm); Lucide/Teo use subtle fade/rise-on-scroll and hover states on grid items. No heavy WebGL or scroll-jacking as a default. Discipline to steal: transform/opacity only, motion as pacing not decoration — matches the animate-skill rules.
reduced_motion_a11y: None of the four document explicit prefers-reduced-motion handling or static fallbacks [uncertain]. Webflow scroll interactions do not respect OS reduced-motion by default unless the builder adds a reduced-motion variation manually, so this is a known gap to fix in a hand-built version. Keyboard/focus and contrast not specified in the source material [uncertain]. For the ECG animation and clinical credibility, treat reduced-motion as a build requirement these templates do not model.
project_presentation: BERGEN/Mokat present work as oversized-type magazine spreads: large project title breaking the grid, full-bleed imagery, wide-tracked caption metadata (title / role / year), each case study reading like a magazine plate rather than a card. Lucide/Teo use a storytelling grid of selected work that opens into structured case-study pages with alternating text/image sections. The stealable pattern for Madhavi: caption-as-metadata block (title . stack/domain . year) under each artifact, and a two-tier index (featured spreads + a compact list for the rest).
research_artifact_presentation: No native papers/publications/talks/citation components in any of the four [uncertain]. Closest reusable pattern is the caption metadata block (title . category . year) mapping onto research metadata (title . venue . year), plus a CMS collection that could host publication write-ups with PDF/URL link rows. There is no built-in venue/citation/GRADE-style component — that must be built (kozodoi's filterable publications index is the better model).
writing_blog_integration: All are Webflow CMS-driven, so a blog/writing collection ships or is trivially added alongside the work collection — case studies and writing edited from one CMS, published side by side with SEO metadata. Lucide/Teo commonly include a blog/journal surface as a first-class nav peer; BERGEN/Mokat can host writing via the same CMS. This models the work+writing fusion (like Sharp/leerob) but via Webflow rather than MDX — for Madhavi the equivalent is MDX collections under one design system.
photography_imagery: Image-forward but framed by type: full-bleed plates with wide-tracked captions (BERGEN/Mokat) so imagery reads as curated, not decorative; Lucide/Teo balance imagery within a storytelling grid. Consistent aspect ratios within a row, generous surrounding whitespace. The stealable rule matches Brand_Kit's photography section: caption every image with restrained metadata and keep one visual identity (same background/accent/type) so a gallery never introduces a new theme.
navigation: Wordmark top-left, short editorial nav (Work / About / Journal / Contact), low item count, often a footer sitemap. BERGEN/Mokat may add an oversized-type or overlay menu for drama; Lucide/Teo keep a minimal fixed top nav. All keep the name top-left and items few — consistent with the Work · Photography · Writing · About · Contact order Madhavi needs.
trust_credibility: Credibility via curation and editorial polish rather than badge walls — selected-work framing, About/manifesto sections, client/press logos kept in About or footer, not the hero. Prose-stated experience and social links sit low on the page. None clutter the hero, matching the Brand_Kit rule to surface affiliations (nference, IIT, MBBS, IAF) without crowding the opening.
contact_conversion: CMS templates funnel to a dedicated Contact page and/or an 'Available for work' status + email CTA in the footer; some include a contact form. No built-in Cal.com booking in these four [uncertain]. Pattern to steal: one primary action per page (Brand_Kit rule) — a copy-to-clipboard email + 'available' status pill rather than five competing links.
performance_weight: Webflow gives solid baseline performance and responsive image handling out of the box; the type-heavy Lucide/Teo builds are light, while media-heavy BERGEN/Mokat spreads depend on image discipline. No published Core Web Vitals or font-loading (FOUT) strategy for these four specifically [uncertain]; a hand-built Next.js version must handle variable-font (Fraunces/Inter) FOUT and image optimization itself rather than relying on the platform.
takeaway: STEAL: the oversized-type magazine-spread project page (BERGEN/Mokat) — a large title breaking the grid over full-bleed media with a wide-tracked caption metadata line (title . stack/domain . year) — plus Lucide/Teo's disciplined storytelling grid and single-CMS work+writing fusion. This gives dense founder-friendly case studies while staying editorial. AVOID: leaning on the platform for accessibility — none handle prefers-reduced-motion, so build the ECG/scroll fallbacks by hand; and avoid any template's standing bold accent competing with the work — keep near-monochrome and let maroon be the only <5% accent.
